newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian ATX up two percent at new closing high.
newsitem.headline: Austrian ATX up two percent at new closing high.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index overcame a lacklustre start on Monday to end two percent up at a new record close and just short of the intra-day high.

Traders traced the bulk of the gains to positive international leads and a dollar at a 7-1/2 year high. Local corporate news and a "buy" recommendation for carton board maker Mayr-Melnhof also played a part, they added.
The 21-share ATX ended 28.83 points up at 1,464.13 -- the highest close since the index was recalculated in January 1991. Earlier it peaked at 1464.43.
"The market has plenty of strength," said one trader, predicting that the ATX would establish itself in a 1,460-1,480 points range.
Top gainer was Mayr-Melnhof, surging over 10 percent to 788 schillings amid talk a British brokerage had issued a "buy" recommendation.
"There was a lot of money behind today's move," a dealer said, pointing to volume of 87,791.
Shares in Bank Austria and Creditanstalt received a boost from strong first-half earnings data.
Creditanstalt ordinaries advanced five percent to a new year high of 894 schillings, followed by a 2.57 percent rise in preference shares to 578.
Bank Austria preferred closed 1.8 schillings higher at 439.8 but ordinaries were steady at 630.
The leading decliner was VA Stahl, down 0.66 percent at 605 schillings.
August ATX futures firmed 31 points to 1,470 on 879 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12254
